items.summary: One person can now direct a team of AI agents that research, write, code and check each other's work. This article examines multi-agent automation: what it does to productivity, where quality control breaks, who is responsible for the output, and what it means to 'manage' work you did not do.
items.title: The Age of AI Agents: One Human, Many Minds

items.summary: The machine writes working code in seconds, so what remains of the programmer? This article looks at how the role is shifting: from typing code to defining problems, from knowing syntax to judging systems, and why the boundary between automation and engineering skill is moving rather than disappearing.
items.title: When AI Writes Code: What Is a Programmer Worth?

items.summary: Trillions are invested, valuations soar, and every product announces intelligence. Is this the internet of 1995 or the tulips of 1637? This article examines how to think about AI hype: the difference between a bubble and a revolution, what real economic value looks like, and how inflated expectations can coexist with genuine technology.
items.title: AI Bubble or Real Revolution?

items.summary: Run a free model on your own machine, own the weights, keep your data — so you are independent now, right? This article examines the illusion of technological self-sufficiency: what local AI really frees you from, what it does not, and why the ecosystem underneath matters more than the model on your disk.
items.title: Free AI and the Illusion of Control

items.summary: Describe an app to an AI, get working code, ship it tonight. Vibe coding is real and it works — until it doesn't. This article explains what is actually happening when software appears from prompts, where technical debt hides in AI-generated code, and why the person who ships is still responsible for what they shipped.
items.title: Vibe Coding and the Illusion of Understanding
